B: Hiya! Can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah. Tracey.
B: Gemma. Nice to meet you, Tracey. How are you getting on with all these?
A: Alright. They're quick, aren't they. You just get going and it's over.
B: I know! I've been talking about pie barms all day, I think I've been rumbled as a Wiganer.
A: The Birmingham lad said. He told me about it. I'd have one.
B: See, that's two of us. What do you do, Tracey?
A: Kitchen assistant. Primary school canteen in Dagenham.
B: Oh, no way, I'm a primary teacher! Year 4. And my mum was a dinner lady before she went TA, so I've grown up hearing all about the kitchen side.
A: Then you'll know the teachers are the worst at the hatch.
B: Oh, we are. We're terrible. I'm sorry on behalf of all of us.
A: It's fine. It's the ones who want something different every day. Jacket potato, no beans, cheese on the side. We ran out of jackets again this week and I had a teacher look at me like I'd done it on purpose.
B: That's not on. Honestly, I always tell our new staff, be nice to the kitchen, they're the ones who know everything that goes on in that school.
A: We do and all.
B: Have you got kids yourself?
A: Dean, he's twenty-seven. Moved out three years ago to Romford with his girlfriend. It was quiet after. Too quiet, if I'm honest. I didn't know what to do with myself for a bit.
B: Oh, I can imagine. Lily's only eleven and she's starting high school in September, and I'm already a bit, you know. It's just me and her. I don't like thinking about her going.
A: You get used to it. Sort of. He rings on a Sunday.
B: That's something.
A: It is. So what do you do for dinner of a night, with her?
B: Tea, you mean? Sorry, I'm being northern. Spag bol, fajitas, I do a big chilli on a Sunday so I'm not cooking when I've got marking.
A: Same, spag bol, shepherd's pie. Roast on a Sunday. I do a big Aldi shop and it's gone up again. Everything's gone up.
B: Don't. The uniform's cost me a fortune and all. The socks have got a logo on.
A: No. That's not right, that. For socks?
B: I said that! I said to the lady, they're socks.
A: They see you coming.
B: They do. Do you watch Gogglebox? You look like a Gogglebox person, sorry, that sounds weird.
A: No, I do. Every Friday with my takeaway. And the soaps. And crime documentaries, which I shouldn't.
B: I fall asleep halfway through anything, I'm useless. I do love Strictly though, with my mum and Lily.
A: I went to a West End show for my fiftieth. Dean paid. I still go on about it.
B: Oh, that's lovely of him. That's a good lad, that.
A: He is. Don't tell him I said.
B: I won't.
